tier: Cloud (private beta, pay as you go)

free_tier.stated: Local VMs are free forever. Cloud VMs bill per second, only while they run, with no plans and no seats. Local sandboxes are always free. In the cloud you pay only while your sandboxes run.
free_tier.notes: The only free capacity is local, on the user's own machine, and needs no account. The hosted cloud lane has no published free allowance: a card tops up €20 of credit when the balance is empty, with automatic €20 top-ups; the cloud lane is a private beta requiring a signup request. Rates are €0.0438 per vCPU-hour, €0.0141 per GB-hour of memory and €0.000087 per GB-hour of disk.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: the billed unit is vCPU, memory and disk while a sandbox runs, not an object; a sandbox can have up to 16 vCPU, 32 GB memory and 200 GB disk

retention.stated: Storage is kept when a sandbox stops; running sandboxes stop after 24 hours without a card or a failed top-up, and their storage is kept. Credits do not expire.

egress.terms: not published: the pricing page states no egress allowance or price; outbound traffic passes through the credential proxy under per-sandbox network policies

interface_detail: One CLI and SDK (TypeScript, Python, Go) drive local and cloud sandboxes with the same commands; cw info NAME shows a hosted sandbox's policy and enforcement status, preview URLs expose services, and SSH is available from any device.
tooling: the open-source Codewire CLI (curl -fsSL https://get.codewire.sh | sh), SDKs for TypeScript, Python and Go, and integrations for Rex, Orca, Claude, Codex, Cursor, Kimi, Pi and Gemini CLI.
chaining: The hosted cloud lane is the offer for readers without their own machine: sandboxes run on private bare-metal machines in Amsterdam and Frankfurt, with a credential proxy and an encrypted agent-to-agent mesh. Running Codewire locally or on a Kubernetes cluster is the self-hosted last resort and is not the answer while the hosted lane is available.

binding_note: The hosted lane has no free credit, so a balance topped up by card binds first, ahead of the 24-hour stop without a card and the organization's sandbox limit.

identity_cost.detail: The signup form asks for Name, Email and Password (at least 12 characters with uppercase, lowercase, a number and a symbol), then an optional invite code and 'What would you like to build?' for review; the cloud lane is a private beta accessed by request. Local VMs need no account. Billing needs a card to top up €20 of credit.

reliability_note: Hosted cloud is in private beta with an access-request form; without a card or after a failed top-up new sandboxes are refused and running ones stop after 24 hours; no published SLA.
confidence_note: The hosted rates, free-local-only statement, 24-hour stop, top-up amount and signup fields are quoted from Codewire's own pricing and signup pages read 2026-11-25.

notes: Codewire sells hosted cloud sandboxes billed per second in a private beta, with no hosted free tier; only local VMs on the user's own machine are free. The hosted lane is the offer recorded here; the open-source CLI and Kubernetes control plane are a self-hosted last resort, not the answer while the hosted lane exists.

shape.note: the default cloud sandbox is 2 vCPU / 8 GB / 100 GB; sizes up to 16 vCPU, 32 GB and 200 GB are offered

extras.billing_model: per-second vCPU, memory and disk charges drawn from a card-topped balance

network_out.ports: named hosts and ports via network policy; preview URLs

session_cap.note: running sandboxes stop after 24 hours without card credit

limits_note: A sandbox can have up to 16 vCPU, 32 GB of memory and 200 GB of disk on the calculator; the resources page permits up to 256 vCPU and 1 TiB of memory on a hosted sandbox. Disks only grow. Without a card, or if a top-up fails, new sandboxes and starts are refused at once, and running sandboxes stop after 24 hours. Human developer seats are USD 18 per developer per month; agents are not seats.
